study.title: Tension-type headache patients' brain responses to instant acupuncture stimulation: a functional magnetic resonance imaging study
study.study_design: Cross-sectional neuroimaging study with within-subject comparison (resting-state vs. acupuncture-state fMRI); two-group design (TTH patients vs. healthy controls)
study.population: Thirty-six TTH patients and thirty-six HCs
study.inclusion_criteria: TTH patients: (1) were 18–65 years old and right-handed; (2) met the diagnosis of TTH based on the International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition in 2018; (3) had a history of TTH for more than 6 months; (4) were able to complete the headache diary independently; (5) had no fear of acupuncture, had no previous history of acupuncture fainting, and agreed to accept intradermal needling; and (6) signed the informed consents by themselves. HCs were recruited to match the age, gender, years of education and handedness of the TTH group.
study.exclusion_criteria: TTH patients were excluded if they: (1) suffered from other types of primary or secondary headache; (2) had any other neurological or psychiatric disorder; (3) were pregnant or breast-feeding; (4) had the contraindications for MRI or acupuncture; or (5) were deemed inappropriate to participate in the trial by the investigators, including poor compliance. HCs had never been diagnosed with head trauma, alcohol/drug abuse, and neurological or psychiatric disorders.

interventions.procedure_label_exact: Instant intradermal acupuncture stimulation at Siguan acupoints
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: Hegu (LI4): dorsum of the hand, midway between the 1st and 2nd metacarpal bones, approximately in the middle of the 2nd metacarpal bone on the radial side. Taichong (LR3): dorsum of the foot, in the depression distal to the junction of the 1st and 2nd metatarsal bones.
interventions.needle_type_exact: HUANQIU disposable press needles; registration number 20162270591
interventions.depth_exact: pressing depth 8–10 mm for LI4 and 5–8 mm for LR3
interventions.manipulation_exact: Each acupoint was pressed 10 times in the order of the left Hegu (LI4), the left Taichong (LR3), the right Taichong (LR3), and the right Hegu (LI4)
interventions.needle_retention_exact: Four intradermal needles were preserved in the four acupoints while the 6-min acupuncture state fMRI scan was proceeding
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: After the fMRI scan, participants were acquired to recall the needling sensations experienced during the acupuncture stimulation fMRI in time, which included sensations associated with the category of Deqi (soreness, numbness, distension, heaviness, or other special sensations) and the sensation with the category of acute pain.

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: Site 1: GE Discovery 750 (Milwaukee, WI, United States) with 16-channel phase-array head coil; Site 2: GE SIGNA Architect (USA) with 19-channel phase-array head coil
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: 3D-T1: spoiled gradient-recalled sequence; BOLD-fMRI: gradient-recalled echo planar imaging (31 contiguous slices)
neuroimaging_methods.TR_exact: 3D-T1: repetition time = 6.008 ms; BOLD-fMRI: repetition time = 2,000 ms
neuroimaging_methods.TE_exact: 3D-T1: echo time = 1.7 ms; BOLD-fMRI: echo time = 30 ms
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: 3D-T1: 1 mm3; BOLD-fMRI: spatial normalization parameter set to 3mm × 3mm × 3mm; slice thickness = 5 mm; field of view = 240 × 240 mm2; data matrix = 64 × 64
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 6 min resting-state; 6 min acupuncture-state; total volumes = 205
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: MATLAB R2021a (Mathworks, Natick, MA, United States) and DPABI V8.0
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: SPM12 (Wellcome Department of Imaging Neuroscience, London, UK)
neuroimaging_methods.coordinate_space_reported_exact: MNI (Montreal Neurological Institute coordinates reported in tables)
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: ALFF and fALFF: smoothed with 6 mm full width at half maximum (FWHM); ReHo: smoothed with 8 mm FWHM
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: Subjects with head motion or translation greater than 2.0° or 2.0 mm were excluded
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: Family-wise error correction (FWE) with a threshold of p < 0.05, and cluster sizes > 30
neuroimaging_methods.source_location: Methods: MRI data acquisition and Statistical analysis of MRI data, pages 3-4

extraction_notes.note: No sham/placebo acupuncture condition is included in this study. The study compares resting-state vs. acupuncture-state within each group only. There is no between-group (TTH vs. HC) neuroimaging contrast table reported.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding measures are not assessed or reported in this study.
Adverse events are not explicitly reported in the paper. No adverse event section is present.
Long-term therapeutic effects of acupuncture (e.g., duration of headache relief or sustained changes in brain activity) were not assessed. Authors explicitly note this as a limitation.

The paper reports 'three patients had same scores for composite Deqi sensation and acute pain' in the TTH group and 'four HCs had the same scores for composite Deqi sensation and acute pain.' These subjects were not included in either subgroup analysis. It is unclear whether they were excluded or assigned to one group.
extraction_notes.source_location: Results: Brain functional activities influenced by different needling sensation, page 5

extraction_notes.note: The coordinate space is labeled MNI in table headers but not explicitly stated in the methods section. The inference is based on standard practice with SPM12 and the label 'Montreal neurological institute' in table footnotes.

The depth_mm_numeric field for needle insertion is not straightforwardly numeric because two different acupoints have different ranges: 8-10mm for LI4 and 5-8mm for LR3. A single numeric value was not assigned.
The fALFF analysis for HCs shows 'No results' for the acupuncture state > resting state direction. This is a null result and has been preserved as a narrative_only contrast.

The between-group neuroimaging comparison (TTH vs. HC) is discussed in the text but no separate between-group contrast table is provided. The paper discusses differences narratively (e.g., TTH-specific ACC and caudate nucleus activation) by comparing within-group results across groups rather than formal between-group statistical testing.

The paper states that data were acquired from two MRI centers with the same parameter settings and harmonized using the shift correction algorithm (SMA). Site effects correction was applied but the normalization template used in SPM12 preprocessing is not explicitly stated.
extraction_notes.source_location: Methods: MRI data acquisition and Statistical analysis of MRI data, pages 3-4

extraction_notes.note: The PMID for this article is not reported in the provided PDF. The article was published online 02 September 2025.
The flip angle for the 3D-T1 sequence is not explicitly reported. Only the BOLD-fMRI flip angle (90°) is provided.

Sensation subgroup classification (predominant acute pain vs. predominant Deqi) was based on post-scan recalled scores, not concurrent ratings. Participants were trained pre-scan with verbal descriptions and visual analog scale practice to differentiate categories.

TTH patients were required to be headache-free for at least 72 hours before and after the fMRI scans. The exact headache-free status at the time of scanning is not verified by any biological or objective measure beyond diary self-report.
